title: MDN JavaScript Guide
description: The definitive JavaScript reference, maintained by browser vendors. Best used as both a first read-through and a lookup reference later.

title: javascript.info — The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
description: A deep, well-structured tutorial covering JS fundamentals through advanced topics like closures, prototypes, and async patterns, with exercises after each chapter.

title: Eloquent JavaScript (free online book)
description: A project-based free book by Marijn Haverbeke. Denser than most tutorials, but builds real problem-solving intuition rather than just syntax familiarity.

title: freeCodeCamp — JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures
description: Interactive, project-based certification covering JS fundamentals plus basic algorithmic thinking. Free, with a real certificate at the end.

title: The Odin Project — Foundations
description: Full open-source curriculum covering HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals through projects rather than isolated lessons.

title: You Don't Know JS Yet (free book series)
description: A free, deeply technical book series on how JavaScript actually works under the hood — scope, closures, this, prototypes, async. The go-to once tutorials stop being enough.

title: TypeScript Official Handbook
description: The official documentation. Start with 'The Basics' — written for people who already know JavaScript and just need the type system explained.

title: TypeScript Deep Dive
description: A free, long-running gitbook that goes past the handbook into practical patterns — generics, utility types, and common gotchas.

title: Total TypeScript — Free Tutorials
description: Short, sharp interactive exercises focused on real type-system problems people actually hit in projects, not toy examples.

title: React Official Docs — Learn React
description: Rewritten with hooks as the default and interactive sandboxes throughout. The correct starting point in 2026 — skip any tutorial still teaching class components as the default.

title: React Official Docs — Thinking in React
description: A short, practical guide on how to break a design into components and decide where state should live. Read this once you know the basics.

title: freeCodeCamp — Front End Development Libraries
description: Includes a full React module with hands-on projects, part of a free certification track.

title: Scrimba — Learn React
description: Interactive, code-along-in-the-browser format. The free tier covers a solid amount of core React before hitting a paywall.

title: patterns.dev
description: Free guide covering modern React and JavaScript design patterns (compound components, render props, rendering patterns) with visual explanations.

title: Node.js Official Docs
description: The official reference. Not a tutorial — best used to look up specific modules (fs, path, events) once you already understand the basics.

title: freeCodeCamp — Back End Development and APIs
description: Covers Node.js, Express, and MongoDB together through five required projects — close to what this app's own backend actually does.

title: roadmap.sh — Node.js Roadmap
description: A visual, topic-by-topic roadmap where every node links out to a curated resource. Good for seeing what you don't know yet.

title: Express Official Docs — Getting Started
description: Short and to the point. Covers routing, middleware, and the request/response cycle directly from the source.

title: MDN — Express/Node Introduction
description: A full walkthrough that builds one real application (a library catalog) end to end — routing, models, forms, deployment.

title: roadmap.sh — Backend Roadmap
description: Places Express in the context of the whole backend stack — useful for seeing what typically comes next (auth, caching, queues).

title: MongoDB Official Manual
description: The full official reference — CRUD operations, the aggregation pipeline, indexing.

title: MongoDB University — Free Courses
description: Official free courses with certificates, taught by MongoDB itself. Best starting point before diving into the manual.

title: Mongoose Official Docs
description: Schemas, validation, middleware (pre/post hooks), and population — directly relevant if you're using Mongoose the way this app does.

title: SQLBolt
description: Short lessons paired with an in-browser SQL editor. Good for building query-writing muscle memory fast.

title: SQLZoo
description: Wiki-style interactive tutorial with real-world-flavored datasets. Good next step after SQLBolt for more complex joins.

title: Khan Academy — Intro to SQL
description: Video lessons combined with interactive coding challenges. Good if you prefer watching before doing.

title: PostgreSQL Official Tutorial
description: Once you know basic SQL, this walks through a specific real RDBMS — useful for understanding constraints, transactions, and indexes concretely.

title: Pro Git (free book)
description: The canonical free Git book, written by Git's own maintainers. Chapters 1-3 cover everything a placement candidate actually needs.

title: GitHub Docs — Get Started
description: Covers the GitHub-specific workflow on top of Git itself — pull requests, forks, issues.

title: NeetCode Roadmap
description: A structured, pattern-based roadmap through the classic problem types (two pointers, sliding window, DP, graphs) rather than random problem grinding.

title: Striver's A2Z DSA Course Sheet
description: An extremely popular free structured sheet that goes from basic to advanced DSA topics with linked problems for each concept.

title: Tech Interview Handbook
description: Covers algorithm study plans by timeline (short/medium/long), plus behavioral prep and practical interview strategy, not just problems.

title: VisuAlgo
description: Visualizes how data structures and algorithms actually move step by step — useful for building intuition before memorizing implementations.

title: GeeksforGeeks — DSA Self-Paced
description: Extremely widely used free reference covering every DSA topic with explanation plus practice problems side by side.

title: System Design Primer
description: The most-referenced free system design resource on the internet. Organized summaries of core concepts (caching, load balancing, CAP theorem) plus worked example problems.

title: Awesome System Design Resources
description: A curated, actively maintained list of free system design articles, videos, and practice problems, organized by topic.

title: ByteByteGo Blog
description: Visual, diagram-heavy explainers of how real systems (URL shorteners, rate limiters, message queues) are actually built.

title: Awesome Low Level Design
description: Covers OOP fundamentals, design patterns, UML, and concurrency specifically for LLD/machine-coding interview rounds — a different skill from HLD system design.

title: InterviewReady — Low-Level-Design repo
description: Worked LLD implementations of classic machine-coding problems (parking lot, elevator system) with concurrency and design pattern usage explained.

title: patterns.dev — Design Patterns
description: Explains the classic Gang of Four design patterns (singleton, factory, observer, strategy) with modern JavaScript examples.

title: MDN — What is a REST API
description: A concise, correct definition of REST constraints — good for making sure you can explain it precisely, not just vaguely, in an interview.

title: restfulapi.net
description: A deeper dive into REST conventions — status codes, HATEOAS, idempotency — the kind of detail interviewers probe for beyond the basic definition.

title: GraphQL Official Docs
description: The official 'Learn GraphQL' guide — schemas, queries, mutations, resolvers, explained by the spec maintainers themselves.

title: Apollo — Odyssey free courses
description: Free, hands-on courses from Apollo (the most widely used GraphQL client/server toolkit) covering building and consuming GraphQL APIs.

title: Hasura Learn — Fullstack GraphQL Tutorial
description: A free, open-source tutorial series going from GraphQL basics to building a full-stack app with React and Node.js.

title: Next.js Official Docs
description: The official documentation, including the interactive 'Learn Next.js' course covering routing, rendering strategies, and data fetching.

title: Next.js — Learn Course
description: A free, official, project-based course that builds a real dashboard app while teaching App Router, layouts, and data fetching patterns.

title: Docker Official Get Started Guide
description: The official walkthrough — containerizing a real app, understanding images vs containers, and basic Docker Compose.

title: Docker Curriculum
description: A free, well-known beginner-friendly walkthrough that builds and deploys a real static site and two web apps.

title: Kubernetes Official Docs — Tutorials
description: The official tutorials, including 'Kubernetes Basics' — an interactive browser-based walkthrough of deployments, pods, and services.

title: learnk8s — Free Kubernetes Resources
description: A maintained list of free trial and always-free-tier managed Kubernetes clusters, useful for actually practicing without paying.

title: GitHub Actions Official Docs
description: Official documentation for building CI/CD pipelines directly inside GitHub — free for public repos and generous limits for private ones.

title: roadmap.sh — DevOps Roadmap
description: Places CI/CD in context alongside containers, infrastructure, and monitoring — useful for seeing how the whole deployment pipeline fits together.

title: Redis Official Tutorials
description: Official how-to guides including building a real-time chat app with Redis Pub/Sub — directly relevant to caching and rate-limiting use cases.

title: Socket.IO — Get Started Guide
description: The official documentation for the most widely used real-time library on top of WebSockets — covers rooms, namespaces, and scaling with Redis.

title: MDN — WebSockets API
description: Explains the underlying browser WebSocket API that libraries like Socket.IO are built on top of — good for understanding what's actually happening.

title: Python Official Tutorial
description: The official tutorial, written by the Python core team. Dense but accurate — good as a primary reference.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
description: A free, extremely popular beginner book that teaches Python through practical automation projects instead of abstract syntax drills.

title: freeCodeCamp — Scientific Computing with Python
description: Free certification track covering Python fundamentals through five hands-on projects.

title: GeeksforGeeks — Java Programming Tutorials
description: Widely used free reference covering Java syntax, OOP concepts, and collections — commonly the first language taught in Indian CS curricula.

title: Java Design Patterns (repo + site)
description: Real, working Java implementations of every classic design pattern with explanations — pairs well with LLD interview prep.

title: Oracle — Official Java Tutorials
description: The official tutorials from the language's maintainer, covering the fundamentals through generics and concurrency.

title: cplusplus.com Reference & Tutorial
description: A long-standing free C++ reference and tutorial — commonly used alongside DSA prep since most competitive programming is done in C++.

title: GeeksforGeeks — C++ Programming Language
description: Covers STL (Standard Template Library) in depth — vectors, maps, sets — which is essential for writing efficient DSA solutions quickly in interviews.

title: MDN — Learn HTML
description: Structured, example-driven lessons on semantic HTML — the foundation everything else in frontend sits on top of.

title: freeCodeCamp — Responsive Web Design
description: Covers HTML, CSS, Flexbox, and Grid through projects, with a free certification.

title: Redux Essentials — Official Tutorial
description: The current official way to learn Redux — uses Redux Toolkit, not the old boilerplate-heavy patterns. Skip any tutorial that doesn't use Redux Toolkit.

title: React Docs — Passing Data Deeply with Context
description: Covers React's built-in Context API — the lighter-weight alternative to Redux for simpler state-sharing needs.

title: Jest Official Docs
description: The most widely used JavaScript testing framework. Start with 'Getting Started' and 'Using Matchers'.

title: Testing Library — React Testing Library Docs
description: The standard way to test React components by interacting with them the way a user would, rather than testing implementation details.

title: OWASP Top 10
description: The official, most-cited list of critical web application security risks (injection, broken auth, XSS) — a near-guaranteed topic in backend interviews.

title: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
description: Concise, practical best practices for specific problems — password storage, JWT handling, input validation — written for developers, not security researchers.

title: MDN — Web Security
description: Covers browser-side security concepts — CORS, CSP, HTTPS — that complement OWASP's more backend-focused material.

title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials
description: Official free introduction to core AWS concepts and services — enough to speak intelligently about cloud basics in an interview.

title: roadmap.sh — DevOps Roadmap
description: Places cloud services in context alongside CI/CD, containers, and infrastructure — useful for seeing how the pieces fit together.

title: GeeksforGeeks — Computer Network Tutorials
description: Widely used free reference covering OSI/TCP-IP models, DNS, and HTTP — the networking basics that show up constantly in interviews.

title: NPTEL — Computer Networks courses
description: Free, university-grade video courses from IITs. Search 'Computer Networks' on the platform for a full-semester-depth free course.

title: GeeksforGeeks — Operating Systems
description: Covers processes, threads, scheduling, and deadlocks — the standard OS interview topic list.

title: NPTEL — Operating Systems courses
description: Search 'Operating Systems' on NPTEL for free, structured, university-depth video lectures.

title: GeeksforGeeks — DBMS
description: Covers normalization, keys, transactions, and ACID properties — the theory side that complements hands-on SQL practice.

title: NPTEL — Database Management System courses
description: Search 'Database Management System' on NPTEL for a free full-depth course covering DBMS theory rigorously.

title: GeeksforGeeks — Object Oriented Programming
description: Covers the four pillars — encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction — with clear examples. A near-guaranteed interview topic.

title: Refactoring Guru — SOLID Principles
description: Clean, visual explanations of SOLID principles and design patterns with before/after code examples — one of the most cited free resources for this topic.

title: MIT — The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
description: A free MIT course covering the command line, shell scripting, and dev tools that most CS courses skip but every job assumes you know.

title: Linux Journey
description: A free, structured, beginner-friendly path through Linux fundamentals — file system, permissions, processes.

title: Codeforces
description: The most active competitive programming platform with regular contests — strong DSA practice under actual time pressure, which mirrors coding-round conditions.

title: LeetCode — Top Interview Questions
description: LeetCode's own officially curated list of 150 classic interview questions, organized by topic — a well-known, reliable starting point.

title: Pramp
description: Free peer-to-peer mock interview platform — you interview a stranger, then they interview you. Genuinely useful for practicing under real conversational pressure.

title: Tech Interview Handbook — Resume Guide
description: Practical, non-salesy resume advice specifically for tech roles — what recruiters actually scan for versus what candidates think they scan for.

title: Tech Interview Handbook — Behavioral Interview Guide
description: Explains the STAR method and gives a structured way to prepare stories in advance instead of improvising under pressure.

title: DataCamp — Software Engineer Interview Questions Guide
description: Covers the newer 2026 interview trend of being asked how you use AI coding tools and how you verify AI-generated output — worth reading since this now comes up often.

title: GitHub Docs — Responsible use of GitHub Copilot
description: Official documentation on how Copilot works and how to review its suggestions critically — useful grounding for questions about verifying AI-generated code.
